title: Phishing part 2: social engineering
sub: Worksheet for the 360° experience: Social engineering HQ
objectives: understand how to identify and protect against phishing
understand the ways people are a weak point
starter: What do we mean by people as a weak point in a secure system?

stations.name: People as a weak point
stations.fact: People are a weak point because...
stations.challenge: List five ways people at your school could accidentally weaken security.

logic.title: Which of these are examples of people being a weak point? Select all that apply.
Why do attackers target people rather than software?

stations.name: Blagging
stations.challenge: Write a blagging script an attacker might use on a school receptionist. How should staff respond?

logic.title: Someone phones claiming to be from IT and asks for your password to 'fix an error'. What should you do?

stations.name: Shouldering and tailgating
stations.challenge: How could a school reduce shouldering at its computers?

logic.title: How does tailgating get someone into a secure building?

stations.name: Baiting
stations.challenge: Why should you never plug in a USB stick you found?

logic.title: You find a USB stick in the car park labelled 'Staff salaries'. What should you do?

stations.name: Phishing, vishing and smishing
stations.challenge: How is vishing different from blagging?

stations.name: Turning people into a strength
stations.challenge: Write three rules you'd put in a school's acceptable use policy.

logic.title: What is an acceptable use policy?
Which is the best defence against social engineering?

final.title: Final challenge: name the technique
final.instr: write your answer for each one.
rows: A caller pretends to be the head teacher and asks for a password reset
Someone stands behind you while you type your PIN
A USB stick labelled 'Exam papers' is left in the corridor
An email claims your account will close unless you log in now
A stranger in a high-vis jacket says they're here to fix the servers
A free game download secretly installs malware
A camera is angled at the keypad by the office door
A text message asks you to confirm your bank details

keyq: What does a phishing attack set out to achieve?
exam: Explain, with examples, why people are often the easiest way into a secure system.
Describe two measures that reduce the risk of social engineering.
confidence: Ways people are a weak point
